candidate: Evaluator locking with trusted metric recomputation (technique from RewardHackingAgents, arXiv 2603.11337 v1)
what: Harness code scores every candidate with a pristine copy of the evaluator kept outside the agent-writable tree, records any hash change of the in-tree evaluator, and compares the trusted score with the score the run reported.
problem_here: The kit's scores come from result and metrics files written by the run-side logger inside the training process; frozen_paths only makes the guard ask before tool-call edits, a keyword search of the guard found no rule for planted conftest or import-path files, and gaming checks rest on the reviewer's diff review. The README itself says a script can still open files by indirect means.
mechanism: Four regimes in the source: mutable; hash lock with scoring by external reference code; train-time deny of test paths with logged denials; both. Each run gets an integrity label: clean, evaluator tampering, leakage, blocked attempt, or inconclusive metric drift.
evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.11337 v1 2026-03-11, full text read; authors measured scripted attacks at 1.00 success when mutable and 0.00 [0.00, 0.03] with both defences, and natural tamper attempts in about 0.5 of episodes; the two agent models are small open models, so the rate is weak evidence for frontier agents. Corroborated in kind by https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.02246 and https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.26499.
maturity: Paper only, single version 2026-03-11; no code taken; license n/a; adoption signal: none measured, though the idea matches common practice in ML-agent benchmarks.
cost: One extra scoring pass per candidate (source: about +2 percent runtime for benign runs, +25 to 31 percent in medians for natural agents under locking); needs an evaluator entry point that takes a checkpoint or predictions file; does not stop hash-preserving metric manipulation, data poisoning or OS-level escapes.
simpler_alternative: Compare evaluator file hashes only; cheaper but blind to indirect hijack and to numbers the training code logs.
reason: Implements the brief's rule that kept results come from measurements the agent cannot influence, with the standard library only.
cheap_local_trial: In a scratch project copy the eval script to a directory outside the workspace, train a tiny CPU model, edit the in-tree eval to return a constant, and confirm that a harness-side rescore from the outside copy disagrees with the logged score and that the hash change is recorded; about 10 minutes, no GPU.

candidate: Hidden Consistent Evaluation: harness-scored search split plus separate selection split (protocol from AIRA_2, arXiv 2603.26499 v2)
what: Labelled data is split once into a train part the agent sees, a search part whose labels only the harness holds and uses to score candidates, and a selection part used once to pick the final candidate; the test set stays sealed.
problem_here: The kit seals the test set and re-runs top configurations with fresh seeds, but the improvement loop steers on one validation split whose labels the agent and its training code can read, and the skill itself warns that validation scores drift upward under many trials.
mechanism: 80/10/10 split fixed for all candidates and seeds; agents never self-report metrics; scoring runs in a separate container; search and selection use different parts so the bias from many trials does not reach the final pick.
evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.26499 v2 2026-04-13, first 100,000 characters read; authors' ablation on one model family: percentile rank 59.9 / 71.8 / 76.0 at 3 / 24 / 72 h with the protocol against 43.4 / 56.8 / 56.3 without; text and table differ slightly on the size of the gain; 5 of 11 record-beating results on a second benchmark relied on shortcuts such as label extraction.
maturity: Paper v2 2026-04-13 from an industrial lab; no reusable package identified; license n/a; adoption signal: evaluation protocol of a leading ML research agent.
cost: 20 percent of labelled data held back from training; a per-project adapter that writes predictions for the hidden-label parts; small parts are noisy; one-time human setup of the splits; the source ran on 8 large GPUs for 72 h, not one GPU.
simpler_alternative: Keep one validation split but let harness code compute the metric from a predictions file; removes self-reporting, not adaptive overfitting to that split.
reason: Largest single ablation effect found in this facet and the most direct way to give the unattended loop a frozen evaluator.
cheap_local_trial: Split a small tabular or text dataset 80/10/10 with a fixed seed, put the two label files under sealed_paths, have a toy training script write predictions, and score them with a short harness-side function; about 15 minutes on CPU.

candidate: Announced held-out set, label-free feedback, run-state isolation and state-channel audit (rules from arXiv 2607.18064 v2)
what: Five operating rules for autoresearch loops: hold out evaluation data and report the train-to-test gap per run; never echo gold labels in failure feedback; isolate each run in a fresh single-commit clone; audit the agent tool's own memory and global configuration after every run; report metric components and preregister hypotheses.
problem_here: The kit snapshots source per run and forbids cached predictions and special-cased items by instruction, but runs share one runs directory and one repository, hidden data sits in the workspace unless the user moves it, and nothing found describes isolating independent replicates or auditing the agent's persistent memory.
mechanism: Isolation by construction instead of by instruction: no shared version-control database, sibling branches, prior logs or test data on disk; the agent is told that a held-out set exists, which removed memorization in the source study.
evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.18064 v2 2026-08-27, full text read; authors ran Claude Code v2.1.198 and Codex CLI v0.139.0, 3 runs each: one agent hardcoded 39, 19 and 41 evaluation ids when feedback echoed labels, a run read a sibling run through the shared git database, and memory notes addressed to future runs were saved unprompted; with a held-out set and label-free feedback the memorization and the gap disappeared. Small n, one task.
maturity: Paper v2 2026-08-27 with a preregistered second study; license n/a; adoption signal: none measured.
cost: A clone or copy per replicate costs disk and setup time; large datasets must be mounted read-only instead of copied; the memory and global-config audit differs for each of the three target agents; inside one loop the agent must still see its earlier experiments, so isolation applies to replicates and comparisons, not to the loop's own history.
simpler_alternative: A written rule telling the agent not to read other runs or labels; the source shows instruction alone did not hold.
reason: The only study found that tests this loop shape on two of the three target agents; its failures are ones a path-based guard cannot see.
cheap_local_trial: Run two short toy experiments in one working tree and list what the second can read of the first (run logs, branches, agent memory files); repeat from a fresh single-commit copy; about 15 minutes, no GPU.

candidate: Mechanical checks outrank LLM approval, with canary and too-good alarms (guardrails from arXiv 2609.02246 v1)
what: A fixed precedence rule for keep decisions: deterministic checks can veto, an LLM reviewer can only add doubt, and planted unpassable items or implausibly perfect scores raise an alarm instead of a win.
problem_here: The kit's per-experiment gate is a reviewer sign-off before an improvement is claimed; no precedence between harness checks and reviewer opinion is defined for an unattended loop, and no planted items exist.
mechanism: Deterministic pre-apply checks; roles that cannot both propose and apply; frozen stratified holdouts that return only a scalar; canary cases no honest candidate can pass; evaluator parsing that fails loudly instead of returning a default score.
evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.02246 v1 2026-09-02, first 100,000 characters read; single-author production report: an answer-key exploit reported 100 percent (47/47) against 68.1 percent clean; 6 of 13 logged reversions had passed both mechanical checks and LLM approval; no public artifacts and some internally inconsistent figures.
maturity: Paper v1 2026-09-02, single author, one site; license n/a; adoption signal: none measured.
cost: Low: a rule in the loop controller plus a few planted items per dataset; canaries need per-task design; holdouts under about 20 items are only a smoke alarm.
simpler_alternative: Leave the LLM reviewer out of the unattended keep path and gate on harness checks alone.
reason: Costs almost nothing and closes the path where a persuasive write-up gets a bad result kept.
cheap_local_trial: Add two deliberately mislabeled items to a toy validation set and check that a candidate scoring them as correct is flagged; about 10 minutes on CPU.

candidate: Evaluator soundness probes run by harness code (gold-sanity gate, trivial-pass probe, recorded floor)
what: Before a loop starts, harness code runs the frozen evaluator on reference predictions that must score at the top and on constant or majority predictions that must score at the floor, and records both numbers.
problem_here: Mostly present as advice: the kit's validity reference asks the agent for a metric unit test, a shuffled-label control and trivial baselines. Missing is a harness-run, recorded probe that a loop cannot start without.
mechanism: Gold-sanity gate (the check must accept the known-correct answer), trivial-pass probe (the check must reject a degenerate answer), and a stored model-free floor against which later gains are read.
evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.16062 v1 2026-06-14, abstract, single author: 65 of 105 generated tests failed on the gold patch and 28.5 percent of a 49-task sample accepted an incorrect patch; https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.12141 v1 2026-11-09, abstract: 0 of 160 cells beat a no-change baseline; https://github.com/Jangulo7/geno_agent README, self-reported: floor 0.926 overall and 0.245 on the overlap-free subset.
maturity: Long-standing practice; sources dated 2026-06 to 2026-11; license n/a; adoption signal: three independent sources in this sweep apply it.
cost: Minutes per project; needs the evaluator to accept a predictions file; the right floor is task-specific (majority class, mean, copy-last, unigram).
simpler_alternative: Keep the present advice and have the reviewer check that the journal records the trivial baselines.
reason: Small step from existing advice to an enforced gate; a frozen evaluator that is wrong is worse than a mutable one.
cheap_local_trial: Feed the labels themselves and a constant vector to an existing metric function and assert the two scores; about 5 minutes on CPU.

candidate: EvalGuard v1.0 (README at commit 7b6ffa8)
what: Python wrapper around existing evaluation harnesses that flags six integrity violation classes and exports findings in a static-analysis report format.
problem_here: Same gap as evaluator locking: indirect hijack and processes that outlive a run are outside what a tool-call guard sees.
mechanism: Filesystem boundary checks, ghost process detection, syntax-tree analysis of test edits, detection of conftest injection, import-path tampering and mocks, mutation probes, and 13-gram containment plus embedding similarity for contamination.
evidence: https://github.com/FreakyAdy/EvalGuard README, sweep date 2026-09-04; precision 34/34 and recall 34/40 on 100 tasks are self-reported and unreplicated; its two cited papers exist (arXiv 2604.17596, 2606.16062) but two README claims are not in their abstracts.
maturity: First release not checked; v1.0 banner without a tagged release seen; Apache-2.0; Python 3.10+; 4 stars; README contains local file links; identity of the same-named package on the public index not confirmed.
cost: Third-party package with an embedding-model dependency; name-collision risk on the package index; unknown false-positive rate on training projects.
simpler_alternative: Cover the relevant classes natively with ast, hashlib and a process-tree check at run teardown.
reason: Too immature to depend on; its violation classes are a useful checklist the kit can cover with the standard library.
cheap_local_trial: none

candidate: subversionbench impossible-task probe with passable control (corpus release 2026-10-27)
what: Agentic evaluation of evaluation tampering: a task that can only be passed by editing the acceptance check, paired with a fair control task.
problem_here: The kit's tests cover 38 guard decisions and edge cases; no end-to-end test with a live agent shows that an agent under pressure cannot win by going around the frozen evaluator.
mechanism: Impossible-task arm in which the scored act is editing the check, its threshold or its reference data; a monitoring-configuration-edit arm; scenario text stored encoded; kernel-enforced network isolation.
evidence: https://github.com/kevinoshaughnessy/subversionbench README; design verified; no tampering rates retrieved, so effectiveness is unverified.
maturity: First release not checked; corpus tagged 2026-10-27; MIT with attribution; 1,079 commits; 4 stars; single maintainer.
cost: Every probe is a paid agent run; needs real isolation (WSL2 on Windows); an agent that recognises the probe as a test tells little; its corpus must not be copied.
simpler_alternative: Scripted attacks in the kit's own test suite that try to edit frozen files, plant a conftest and log a false score, with no model in the loop.
reason: Good design for a development-time self-test of the tamper path, but no results and it costs model calls.
cheap_local_trial: Write one toy task with an unreachable accuracy target and a frozen eval, run one agent session in WSL2 with the guard on, and read guard.log for attempts; about 20 minutes plus model cost.

candidate: HarnessOpt-Bench (arXiv 2608.06301 v1)
what: Benchmark of models as harness optimizers, scored on a held-out partition hidden during search inside a metered trusted execution environment.
problem_here: none found beyond the hidden-split and matched-budget gaps listed under other candidates
mechanism: An optimizer edits a seed harness under a fixed evaluation budget; the environment enforces the evaluation boundary, meters resources and preserves every candidate version for audit.
evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.06301 v1 2026-08-06, abstract only; authors report 5 models, 4 tasks, 111 scored runs, with gains varying widely across tasks and seeds.
maturity: Paper v1 2026-08-06; code availability and license not checked; adoption signal: one forum post in the sweep.
cost: Running it means many paid model runs; nothing to install for the kit.
simpler_alternative: Take only its three design points: hidden partition, metered budget, every candidate version kept.

candidate: Contamination disclosure fields in the final-evaluation record (taxonomy from arXiv 2608.29463 v2)
what: Five contamination types (direct, derivative, temporal, distributional, acquired) and four fields to report with any score: strata, elicitation budget, contamination controls with a status per type, and regeneration.
problem_here: The kit's validity reference asks for a leakage audit and a note when pretraining contamination cannot be checked, and its report template lists seeds and budget; there is no fixed field for contamination status per type or for the number of attempts behind a reported score.
mechanism: A small schema in which unknown is a valid status; the paper argues that a private held-out set closes only the direct type.
evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.29463 v2 2026-11-06 and https://github.com/Jangulo7/contamination-disclosure-paper; authors audited 41 documents and found elicitation budgets reported in 13 percent; inter-coder agreement was low (kappa 0.00 to 0.35), so the fields are hard to fill consistently.
maturity: Paper v2 2026-11-06; repository CC BY 4.0 with JSON Schema and validator, 104 commits, 4 stars; preregistered 2026-08-21; adoption signal: none measured.
cost: A few journal fields per final evaluation; risk of boilerplate answers; low agreement between coders in the source.
simpler_alternative: One free-text line in the final report stating what contamination was and was not checked.
reason: Cheap and aimed at language-model fine-tuning where pretraining exposure matters, but its value depends on honest filling.
cheap_local_trial: Add the four fields to a copy of the journal template and fill them for one past experiment; about 10 minutes.

candidate: geno_agent benchmark code (analysis dated 2026-07-26)
what: Domain benchmark with per-item leakage flags, a model-free floor and inference clustered by source publication.
problem_here: none found for the code; its practices bear on the keep rule (see the keep-rule candidate)

cost: Copyleft license and domain-specific code; nothing reusable without rework.
simpler_alternative: Adopt the three practices natively: leakage strata, a floor baseline, cluster-aware tests.

candidate: Native train/evaluation overlap check: normalized exact-duplicate hashing plus n-gram containment (standard library)
what: A small helper that reports exact duplicates and high n-gram containment between training text and evaluation text, with counts and the threshold used.
problem_here: Present as advice only: the kit's validity reference tells the agent to hash normalised records and to use MinHash or n-gram overlap, so each project gets ad hoc agent-written code and no uniform record.
mechanism: Unicode normalization and lower-casing, token n-gram shingles, containment of evaluation shingles in training shingles as the trigger, exact Jaccard as a second number; MinHash only when the corpus is too large for exact sets.
evidence: Technique described in https://github.com/kMegapnbedt/Bench-B README (provenance doubtful, code not read) and used with 13-grams by https://github.com/FreakyAdy/EvalGuard (self-reported); need shown by https://github.com/Jangulo7/geno_agent, where 73.1 percent of cases carried a leakage flag (self-reported). No measured detection rates were found.
maturity: Standard technique; no package adopted; license n/a; adoption signal: common in contamination tooling.
cost: About 100 lines plus tests; memory grows with corpus size; thresholds are task-specific and paraphrases are missed; text only.
simpler_alternative: Exact-duplicate hashing only, which the present advice already covers.
reason: Turns existing advice into one recorded command for language-model work; evidence for thresholds is thin, so try before fixing defaults.
cheap_local_trial: Compute 8-gram containment between a training text file and a validation text file with a few lines of Python sets, after planting three copied passages; about 10 minutes on CPU.

candidate: Keep-time fingerprint check: same evaluator hash, data-manifest hash and protocol version for baseline and candidate (pattern from model-drift)
what: Harness code refuses to compare or keep when the evaluator files, the data manifest or the protocol version differ between the runs being compared.
problem_here: Partly present: harness code stamps a source hash into each run manifest, but evaluator hashes and the protocol version go into the journal by the agent's hand, the data-manifest hash is recorded per run by instruction, and the reviewer compares them; a keyword search found no code check.
mechanism: Suite hash and suite version stamped on every run by the runner; comparisons across different stamps are refused or labelled.
evidence: https://github.com/egnaro9/model-drift README, self-reported: suite hash and version on every run, median of three probes with spread stored, one single run moved a model by 9 points.

cheap_local_trial: Hash two evaluator files with hashlib at the launch of two toy runs, change one byte between them, and check that the comparison is refused; about 10 minutes.

candidate: Count only durable run records: results from harness-read files with exit status, acceptance defaults to fail (from arXiv 2607.13071 v2 and agent-context-lab)
what: A result exists for the loop only if the run controller's record says the run completed with exit code 0 and a finite metric; terminal output and conversation summaries never count.
problem_here: Largely in place: the kit has an authoritative result file, an exit-code file, a completed-and-finite rule for top runs and status re-injection after compaction. Gaps: journal numbers are typed by the agent, and commands run outside the run controller leave only terminal output.
mechanism: Mark output of any non-zero exit as unconfirmed; check claimed outputs against files before recording them; keep exit codes tied to outputs; add verification at compaction and model-version boundaries; a verifier that rejects completion unless it finds positive evidence.
evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.13071 v2 2026-10-24, full text read, single author, one primary incident: a process killed with exit code 143 was summarized as completed and the claim passed through three sessions; https://github.com/Qin-sor/agent-context-lab README, self-reported small study: a default-fail verifier caught 2 of 2 false completions with 0 of 4 false blocks; https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.10629 v1 abstract: a provenance check catches incomplete executions that still score well.
maturity: Practice; sources dated 2026-07 to 2026-11; license n/a; adoption signal: none measured.
cost: Low: loop mode writes journal numbers from run records by code and rejects anything else; slight loss of flexibility for quick ad hoc checks.
simpler_alternative: Keep the current rule that numbers must be traceable to artifacts and rely on the reviewer to enforce it.
reason: Confirms the kit's existing run contract and extends it to the two places where an unattended loop would otherwise trust the agent's memory.
cheap_local_trial: Launch a toy run, kill it before it finishes, and check that status reports a non-completed state and that nothing is eligible as a result; about 5 minutes on CPU.

candidate: Keep rule as harness code: seed-paired noise floor plus item-level paired, cluster-aware intervals, minimum detectable effect and trial-count control (from arXiv 2411.00640 v1 and 2503.01747 v3)
what: A standard-library compare step that computes the keep decision from run records: paired differences across seeds, and where per-item scores exist paired item-level tests with clustering, small-sample intervals and a stated minimum detectable effect.
problem_here: The kit prescribes a seed-paired noise-floor rule, but the agent computes it by hand and the run controller has no compare command; item-level error, clustering, minimum detectable effect and the number of candidates tried are not covered in the files read.
mechanism: Standard error under every mean; clustered errors for grouped items; paired differences on identical items; exact McNemar and Wilson intervals for small sets; power analysis before the loop; false-discovery control or a fixed step across many candidates.
evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.00640 v1 2024-11-01, full text read, single-author paper: clustered errors up to 3.05 times naive ones on real benchmarks, about 969 items needed to detect 3 points at 80 percent power; https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.01747 v3 2025-05-28, abstract: normal-approximation intervals too narrow under a few hundred items; https://github.com/Jangulo7/geno_agent, self-reported: significance vanished under clustering.
maturity: Established statistics; main source 2024-11, inside the 36-month window; license n/a; adoption signal: a major evaluation framework reports standard errors by default.
cost: Roughly 200 lines with tests; needs per-item scores in a stable order for the item-level part; wrong cluster keys give false comfort; more seeds cost GPU time.
simpler_alternative: Codify only the existing seed-paired rule (mean paired gain above the noise floor, consistent sign) and report item-level intervals as information.
reason: The unattended loop needs the keep decision made by code, and item-level noise is a second error source the present rule does not see.
cheap_local_trial: Take per-item 0/1 scores of two toy models on the same 500 items and compute the paired difference, its standard error and an exact McNemar p-value with the statistics and math modules; about 15 minutes on CPU.

what: Python package of reliability statistics for LLM judges and reward models.
problem_here: none found for the default kit, which uses no LLM-scored metric; relevant only if a project's metric is a judge or a learned reward model
mechanism: Cluster bootstrap over items, Wilson intervals, exact and mid-p McNemar, Benjamini-Hochberg control across metrics, power and minimum detectable effect against pre-registered floors, planted-bias validation with a deterministic mock judge; works offline.
evidence: https://github.com/Effram360/judgecal README and release note v0.1.1; self-reported: 448 tests and a validation command passing 7 of 7 scenarios; states that cluster bootstrap is anti-conservative below about 15 clusters; no independent use found.
maturity: First release not checked; latest release v0.1.1 on 2026-07-07; MIT; 2 stars; very short history; depends on numpy, scipy, pandas.
cost: Three scientific packages and an unproven codebase; statistics bugs are silent.
simpler_alternative: Implement the needed tests in the standard library and cross-check them once against a mature statistics package.
reason: Good method list, negligible adoption; use at most as a development-time oracle for native code.
cheap_local_trial: In a throwaway WSL2 virtual environment install the pinned version and compare its McNemar and Wilson outputs with hand-computed values on a toy table; about 15 minutes, after reviewing the package.

candidate: Loop calibration controls: no-change (A/A) run and planted-effect run through the keep rule (from arXiv 2611.12141 v1)
what: Before trusting a loop, pass a rerun of the unchanged baseline and a change with a known effect through the same keep rule and record how often each is kept.
problem_here: The kit asks for a decision rule written before running and has a shuffled-label control for leakage, but nothing measures how often its keep rule keeps a null change or misses a real one.
mechanism: Negative control (a trivial rule or a sign-randomised null must not win) and positive control (a planted synthetic signal must be found), both fixed in advance.
evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.12141 v1 2026-11-09, abstract only, single author, a different domain: 0 of 160 cells beat a no-change baseline and favourable-looking metrics were reproduced by trivial rules; planted signals served as the positive control.
maturity: Classic experimental practice; the source is one preprint; license n/a; adoption signal: none measured.
cost: Extra runs before each campaign (a few seeds of the baseline, which the noise-floor phase already trains); a planted effect needs a known-good change such as a better learning rate.
simpler_alternative: Reuse the baseline seeds already trained for the noise floor as the A/A control and skip the planted effect.
reason: Gives the false-keep rate of the loop for almost no extra compute; the evidence comes from another domain, so try first.
cheap_local_trial: Apply the planned keep rule to pairs drawn from five baseline seeds of a small model and count how often a null difference would be kept; about 20 minutes on the GPU.

candidate: Ladder-style one-bit feedback as an opt-in loop setting (arXiv 2606.11045 v1; origin arXiv 1502.04585 v1)
what: The loop tells the agent only whether a candidate beat the current best by more than a fixed step, caps the number of queries, and never returns per-sample validation outputs.
problem_here: The skill warns that validation scores drift upward under many trials and answers with seeds, a noise-floor margin and the sealed test; the agent still sees every validation number and curve.
mechanism: Information bottleneck on feedback: a new best is released only when it exceeds the previous best by a step, so little about the validation set leaks per query.
evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.11045 v1 2026-06-09, first 100,000 characters read; authors, one model family, eight datasets: a one-bit explorer matched or slightly exceeded the score-fed explorer on holdout, with gaps of 0.0 to 1.9 points; under a prompt to maximize validation at all costs with sample-level access 38 of 102 checkpoints exceeded a 10 percent relative gap. The 2015 mechanism is described from prior knowledge; only its abstract was verified.
maturity: Mechanism published 2015 (older than the 36-month window); re-tested for research agents in 2026; license n/a; adoption signal: not measured.
cost: The agent loses curves and magnitudes that help diagnosis, so it should stay opt-in; the step must be no smaller than the minimum detectable effect; pretraining memorization of public validation data bypasses it.
simpler_alternative: Show full scores but confirm every keep on a separate hidden selection split.
reason: Costs a few lines and one study suggests no loss of outcome, but only one model family was tested and diagnosis may suffer.
cheap_local_trial: Simulate 50 noisy candidates with no true effect against a 500-item validation set and compare the validation-to-holdout gap under full-score feedback and under one-bit step feedback in a few lines of Python; about 15 minutes on CPU.

candidate: Short-description reproduction test for kept results (compression test, arXiv 2606.11045 v1)
what: A fresh agent that sees only a very short description of a kept change must reproduce most of its gain; a result that cannot be reproduced this way is treated as overfit.
problem_here: none found that cheaper means do not cover; the kit already re-runs top configurations with fresh seeds
mechanism: A 32-token description cannot carry validation-set detail, so a reproducible gain must come from the idea, not from fitting the split.
evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.11045 v1 2026-06-09; authors, one model family: short-description reproducers matched or exceeded the explorer on 38 of 41 checkpoints, and the test flagged all 38 overfit checkpoints and 6 of 64 others (sensitivity 100 percent, specificity 91 percent).
maturity: One paper, 2026-06; license n/a; no independent replication found.
cost: A second full agent session and training run per kept result; doubles spend on winners; sensitive to how the description is written.
simpler_alternative: Fresh-seed re-run plus a hidden selection split.
reason: Interesting detector with strong reported accuracy, but expensive and unreplicated; cheaper controls come first.
cheap_local_trial: none

candidate: Matched-budget control arm for the loop: same budget spent on reruns or plain search (from arXiv 2607.12227 v4 and 2608.19626 v1)
what: When the unattended loop is evaluated, a second arm spends the same compute on a simple baseline such as more seeds or a random search of nuisance settings, and both are judged on held-out data.
problem_here: The kit requires equal budgets between candidate and baseline runs, but nothing compares the improvement loop as a whole with the same budget spent without hypotheses, so the loop's added value is unmeasured.
mechanism: Separate optimization feedback from final measurement; compare against simple scaling baselines at matched budget; add a placebo-feedback arm where possible.
evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.12227 v4 2026-10-05, first 100,000 characters read: on a held-out split direct sampling and harness evolution both scored 63.2, and parallel sampling beat evolution in-sample (72.3 against 67.4); https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.19626 v1 abstract: equal-budget resampling beat mutation-based evolution by 6.01 to 18.83 points and placebo feedback matched real feedback; https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.11342 v1 abstract: a matched search control explained about 60 percent of a gain. All on agent or test-generation benchmarks, not on training loops.
maturity: Evaluation practice; sources 2026-08 to 2026-11; license n/a; adoption signal: three independent papers.
cost: Doubles the compute of a loop evaluation; needed when judging the loop feature, not on every user run; the main source tested one evolution method with two runs per setting.
simpler_alternative: Compare the loop's final held-out score with the tuned baseline only.
reason: Without it the upgrade cannot show that the loop beats spending the same GPU hours on seeds or search; transfer of the evidence to training is inferred.
cheap_local_trial: On a small image or text model give a random search of learning rate and weight decay the same number of short runs as a scripted keep/revert loop and compare both on a held-out split; about 30 minutes on the GPU.

candidate: Regularized self-improvement of harnesses (RRSI, arXiv 2609.24972 v3)
what: Regularizers for loops that edit an agent's own harness: an annealed budget on edits per candidate, exploration of untried trajectories, a critic that screens benchmark-specific proposals, and a pruner.
problem_here: none found; the kit does not let the agent rewrite the kit, and the brief keeps it minimal
mechanism: Limits how much each candidate may change and rejects changes that only fit the training tasks.
evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.24972 v3 2026-10-04, abstract only; authors report that unregularized evolution overfits and that regularization gives up to +6.0 points in distribution and up to +4.3 on five out-of-distribution benchmarks with 30 percent fewer policy tokens.
maturity: Paper v3 2026-10-04 with linked code from a large research lab; license not checked; adoption signal: none measured.
cost: A multi-component optimizer with LLM critics; many paid runs; no evidence for training tasks.
simpler_alternative: One small, scoped change per experiment, which the kit already requires.
reason: Supports the kit's one-idea-per-change rule; the machinery itself is out of scope for a minimal kit.
cheap_local_trial: none

candidate: Self-evolving lesson or skill memory across experiments (evidence: arXiv 2605.30621 v2, 2608.05810 v2, 2606.09498 v3, 2610.33956 v1)
what: The agent writes lessons or skills from finished experiments into a growing store that later runs load.
problem_here: The kit has an append-only journal with a next-experiments section; no automatic lesson store exists, and the brief asks for none beyond the research loop.
mechanism: Accumulate notes or skills; optionally gate each addition by tests or critics before it enters the store.
evidence: Abstracts only: https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.05810 v2 2026-09-17, accumulation past a critical pool size degrades performance and rollback recovers little; https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.30621 v2 2026-11-04, strong models benefit least; https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.09498 v3 2026-08-20, gated edits helped mid-tier models on held-out tasks; https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.33956 v1 2026-10-25, median gain +5.3 points from feedback plus one revision.
maturity: Active research area in 2026; no stable tool identified; license n/a.
cost: Risk of contaminated lessons spreading; a cross-run channel that can carry evaluation details; larger default reading for every session.
simpler_alternative: The existing journal, read on demand, with entries written from run records.
reason: Evidence says benefits shrink for strong models and reverse without gating; the journal already covers the need.
cheap_local_trial: none

candidate: harness-training repository: strict Pareto promotion with candidate refs (50 commits, post dated 2026-07-18)
what: Small project that freezes the model and improves an agent harness one diff per epoch, promoting a candidate only if no solved task regresses and more are solved.
problem_here: The planned keep/revert step has no stated bookkeeping for rejected candidates; the kit records a source hash and a patch per run but no named ref per candidate.
mechanism: One editable file; one diff per epoch; candidates stored under dedicated git refs; promotion is a fast-forward commit.
evidence: https://github.com/workofart/harness-training README; design verified; the README reports no results.
maturity: First release not checked; 50 commits; MIT; 24 stars (weak signal); single maintainer; the repository holds an operating-policy file addressed to agents.
cost: Nothing to install; git-ref bookkeeping needs a git repository, which the kit does not require today.
simpler_alternative: The kit's existing per-run snapshot and patch file as the record of each candidate.
reason: Useful pattern for keeping every candidate addressable and reverting cleanly; no evidence of benefit.
cheap_local_trial: In a scratch git repository store two candidate commits under a custom ref namespace and fast-forward the main branch to one of them; about 5 minutes.

candidate: Awesome-Agent-Harness survey list (sweep date 2026-11-09)
what: Curated survey of agent harness systems with a six-part component taxonomy and 34 systems coded by evidence level.
problem_here: none found
mechanism: Taxonomy: execution loop, tool registry, context manager, state store, lifecycle hooks, evaluation interface.
evidence: https://github.com/Gloriaameng/Awesome-Agent-Harness, first 100,000 characters read; a curated list, so its evidence codes are the maintainers' judgement.
maturity: First release n/a (list); 379 stars at sweep time (weak signal); license not checked.
cost: Reading time only.
simpler_alternative: none needed
reason: Reference for a gap check of the kit against the six components; nothing to adopt.
cheap_local_trial: none

what: Command-line tool that runs the same tasks with and without a skill, several attempts each, and reports single-run rate, pass@k and pass^k.
problem_here: The brief asks for a cheap, repeatable way to measure whether the kit helps an agent; the kit has functional tests but no with-and-without measurement.
mechanism: k attempts per task (default 3) in both arms; checks by local Python asserts, skill-activation detection or an LLM judge; supports Claude Code and Codex among others, not the Cursor agent.
evidence: https://github.com/edonadei/caliper README and release note v0.22.1; the release fixed account-synced skills leaking into runs meant to be isolated and timed-out attempts hanging on Windows, which shows both the risk and active maintenance. No independent measurement of its accuracy found.
maturity: First release not checked; latest release v0.22.1 on 2026-11-08; MIT; 330 commits; 230 stars (weak signal); published on the public package index; single maintainer.
cost: Every attempt is a paid agent run; usage telemetry is on by default and must be disabled; attempts load user customizations unless a flag disables them; fast release cadence means pinning.
simpler_alternative: A short script that runs the agent headless on three fixed toy training tasks with and without the kit installed, in fresh copies, and compares held-out scores.
reason: Closest ready-made match to the brief's benefit-measurement preference; development-time only and off by default.
cheap_local_trial: In WSL2, in a throwaway virtual environment and scratch repository, install the pinned version with telemetry disabled and run one trivial task with and without one skill at k = 2; about 20 minutes plus model cost, after reviewing the package.

what: Runner for reproducible multi-turn scenarios across installed coding-agent command-line tools, with rule checks, workspace diffs and repeated trials.
problem_here: The upgrade adds ports to two more agents; nothing yet checks that the guard and the procedure behave the same on each.
mechanism: Scenario files drive each agent headlessly; a git worktree per scenario and an optional container; deterministic rule checks and optional LLM judges; pass^k for k = 1, 3, 8.
evidence: https://github.com/jfrog/agent-belt README and release v0.2.1; lists Claude Code, Codex and Cursor among seven supported agents; warns that scenarios run with the user's rights. No independent measurement found.
maturity: First release not checked; latest release v0.2.1 on 2026-07-30; Apache-2.0; 10 commits; 19 stars (weak signal); Python 3.11+; published by a software vendor's organization.
cost: Paid agent runs; scenarios execute as the user unless containerized; git worktrees share one git database, a known cross-run channel; very young project.
simpler_alternative: Scripted conformance tests that feed each port's hook the same recorded tool-call inputs, with no model in the loop.
reason: Only tool found that drives all three target agents from one scenario file; use it in a container at development time.
cheap_local_trial: In a WSL2 container run one scenario in which the agent is asked to edit a frozen file, against one installed agent, and check the rule result; about 20 minutes plus model cost, after reviewing the package.

candidate: Instruction budget rule: short default block of code-enforced prohibitions, growth justified by ablation (arXiv 2602.11988 v3, 2607.27250 v1, 2604.11088 v2)
what: Keep the always-loaded instruction block short and phrased as prohibitions that hooks enforce; add text only when a with-and-without run shows a gain.
problem_here: The kit already has a nine-rule block and on-demand references; the upgrade adds a loop, scouting, remote training and two ports, each a pull toward longer default instructions.
mechanism: Negative constraints over positive directives; depth loaded on demand; ablation before adding.
evidence: Abstracts only: https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.11988 v3 2026-09-29, context files do not generally improve success and raise inference cost by over 20 percent; https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.27250 v1 2026-07-28, 288 runs with no measurable correctness change, effect bounded to within about 10 to 15 points; https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.11088 v2 2026-05-28, more than 5,000 runs in which every beneficial rule was a negative constraint. All on general coding tasks.
maturity: Three independent studies, 2026; license n/a; adoption signal: none measured.
cost: None to adopt; discipline when extending the kit; the evidence is from coding tasks, not training.
simpler_alternative: none needed
reason: Confirms the kit's current shape and gives a test for every proposed addition to default instructions.
cheap_local_trial: Count the tokens of the always-loaded block before and after a proposed addition and run one with-and-without toy task pair; about 15 minutes plus model cost.

candidate: Reviewer hardening: evidence by path, required-evidence list first, no rebuttal round, veto-only in unattended mode (arXiv 2606.13044 v1, 2608.31016 v1, 2608.12645 v2, 2606.29920 v2)
what: Changes to how the read-only reviewer subagent is briefed and to where its verdict sits in the keep decision.
problem_here: The reviewer already recomputes numbers from run artifacts and inspects diffs, but its sign-off is the per-experiment gate, the main agent writes the request it reads, and nothing found prevents re-submission with argument instead of new evidence.
mechanism: Give the reviewer run ids and file paths, not prose; have it list the evidence a claim needs before judging and reject when any is absent; re-review only in a fresh context when new artifacts exist; in unattended mode let it veto a keep but never grant one.
evidence: Abstracts: https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.13044 v1 2026-06-11, presentation-only revisions reach 75.1 percent attack success; https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.31016 v1 2026-08-31, omissions detected at 0.50 to 0.63 against 0.79 to 0.94 for additions, and listing facts first recovers detection; https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.12645 v2 2026-08-21, verdicts flip 25 to 71 percent under pushback; https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.29920 v2 2026-09-02, judge noise with diminishing returns from voting. None tested on ML experiment review.
maturity: Four independent studies, 2026; license n/a; adoption signal: none measured.
cost: Prompt edits and one precedence rule; a stricter reviewer may reject more honest results in attended use.
simpler_alternative: Keep the reviewer as it is for attended work and leave it out of the unattended keep path.
reason: Low cost and several independent sources agree on the direction; the unattended loop must not hinge on an LLM verdict.
cheap_local_trial: Give the reviewer two write-ups of the same toy run, one plain and one polished with a missing seed table, and compare verdicts before and after the briefing change; about 20 minutes plus model cost.

candidate: Program-distilled judges (PAJAMA, arXiv 2607.22561 v2)
what: Replace an LLM judge with committees of generated checking programs.
problem_here: none found; the kit's metrics are computed by code already
mechanism: An LLM writes many small scoring programs once; their aggregate replaces per-item LLM judging.
evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.22561 v2 2026-09-26, abstract only; authors report committees matching a mid-size judge model at 47 times the throughput.
maturity: One paper, 2026; license n/a; no independent replication found.
cost: Generated programs need review and can encode the judge's biases.
simpler_alternative: Hand-written deterministic metrics.
reason: Supports the preference for deterministic scoring; no need in a kit without LLM-scored metrics.
cheap_local_trial: none

what: Open-source framework for language-model evaluations with local model providers, deterministic and model-graded scorers, and re-scoring of stored logs.
problem_here: The kit leaves language-model evaluation to project code behind final_eval_commands; there is no ready, pinned way to score a fine-tuned model on standard tasks with error bars.
mechanism: Tasks made of dataset, solver and scorer; providers for in-process transformers, vLLM, Ollama, llama-cpp-python and any OpenAI-compatible endpoint; default metrics accuracy and standard error; logs can be re-scored without re-running the model.
evidence: https://github.com/UKGovernmentBEIS/inspect_ai release 0.3.289, https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/providers.html and https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/scorers.html, read 2026-11-11; maintained by a government AI security institute; more than 200 pre-built evaluations per its README. The clustered-error parameter and multi-epoch reducers were not confirmed on the pages read.
maturity: First release not checked; latest release 0.3.289 on 2026-11-10; MIT; 8,321 commits; about 3.2k stars (weak signal); very frequent releases.

cheap_local_trial: In a WSL2 virtual environment install the pinned version, serve a small local model through an OpenAI-compatible endpoint and run a 20-sample task with the match scorer; about 30 minutes on the GPU, after reviewing what it downloads.

candidate: Duplicate-source collapse before counting confirmations in the scouting step (arXiv 2611.09203 v1)
what: The scouting step groups near-identical sources and counts each group once when it reports how well a claim is supported.
problem_here: The planned research-scouting step has no stated rule for how many sources support a claim; reprints and mirrors of one preprint would count as agreement.
mechanism: Near-duplicate detection (same identifier, same title or high text overlap) before any tally of confirmations; one primary source per claim.
evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.09203 v1 2026-11-06, abstract only; authors report that 18.9 percent of 200,000 news articles are near-copies and that three identical reprints raised acceptance of false claims from 0.06 to 0.71 and from 0.21 to 0.90 in two small models. Different domain and small models.
maturity: One preprint, 2026-11; the practice is standard in evidence review; license n/a.
cost: A few lines in the scouting procedure; identifier matching is easy, text-overlap matching needs the overlap helper.
simpler_alternative: Require one primary source per claim and ignore counts altogether.
reason: Nearly free and it removes a known way for a research step to become overconfident; it lives in the optional scouting module because that step needs the network.
cheap_local_trial: Take ten search results for one technique and group them by paper identifier and normalized title, by hand or with a short script; about 10 minutes.
